registerNotes: Everyday, unmarked Peninsular verb meaning to take/catch. Its vulgar LatAm meaning does not apply in Spain and must not be taught as the meaning here.

senses.gloss: to take, to catch (a bus, a train)
senses.example: Coge el autobús a las ocho.

senses.gloss: to pick up, to take (an object)
senses.example: Coge el pan de la mesa.
senses.exampleGloss: Take the bread from the table.

alternatives.reason: Shared synonym, common in Peninsular usage too; slightly more neutral.
Stronger grip; usable in Spain but blunter than coger.
Colloquial Peninsular; right for catching a train at the last second.

notes: Correct and unmarked in Spain; the registerNotes exist so the reviewer sees the LatAm vulgar-meaning trap was considered.
